x: The 100 yards boys' race saw Ken Eales score an easy win and it was interesting to see the sons of Jack and Joe Flower, two old club champions, competing in this event.
He sends best wishes to all old pals and in particular to Frank Thomson. Joe Flower writes to say that he hopes to be at the Championship meeting and wishes to be remembered to all old friends.
For the first time we included in our team Arthur Allum and Arthur Penny (both to win International cross-country honours later) and the brothers Jack and Joe Flower.

And ALBERT WATTAM in Lincolnshire, TOMMY GREEN (our 1932 Olympic Champion) in Hampshire, STAN VICKERS, the CHURCHERS, DON BROWN at Richmond, JOE FLOWER and BERT MITCHELL in Kent ? - And the many others who have added something to the Belgrave story in the years that are passed ?
How pleasant to see JOE FLOWER, now retired, at our Track Championships----but a little chastening to be reminded that it was 40 years earlier that he had won the Mile Championship!
Joe Flower led the field for a lap at a pace which suggested he had no intention of completing the distance - a suggestion which, of course, was soon confirmed.
Joe Flower's son writes to inform us of his father's recent death. Joe was one of our leading runners in the twenties and thirties and was a former one mile Club Champion.

Joe Flower, writing from West Africa, says of 'The Belgravian' ``What pleasure that little journal brings''. Dan Patience, after having been stationed in the wilds of Ayr, bemoaning his fate because he couldn't get a run, now writes from North Africa!

Joe Flower carried on the good work, overhauling Highgate and Tipton and bringing us up to third. Bert Footer ran next and although he ran faster than any other Belgrave man has done in the past over this stretch, he was forced to surrender places to Tipton H. and Surrey AC.
